ostracism

/OS-truh-siz-uhm/ - the stress falls on OS · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Ostracism means exclusion from a group by deliberate shunning.

New hires who skipped the union picnic learned that a season of quiet ostracism could be colder than any reprimand.

Example

Naturalists describe ostracism among ravens: a bird that steals from the shared cache is driven to the edge of the roost, and for weeks none of the others will feed beside it.

Ostracism is more specific than rejection because it is exclusion enforced by the group's own behavior — no ruling, no announcement, just a closing of ranks that leaves one member outside them.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

exclusion: Exclusion is the broadest term for being left out — by rule, by chance, or by design, once or always. Ostracism is one specific kind: deliberate, sustained shunning by a group of one of its own, enforced through cold behavior rather than any written rule.

shunning: Shunning is the pointed avoidance itself — the turned backs, the unreturned greetings — and a single person can shun another. Ostracism is that treatment organized and sustained: a whole group closing ranks against one member and keeping the freeze going for weeks.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

acceptance: being taken in as one of the group

welcome: the warm reception an outsider hopes for

Where it sits · how far the group's rejection goes — snub → ostracism → banishment

snub vs. ostracism: A snub is a single icy moment — one greeting refused, one invitation withheld; ostracism is that treatment organized and sustained by the whole group.

banishment vs. ostracism: Banishment goes further than ostracism: the group does not merely freeze you out of its company, it formally casts you out of the place itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ostrac

Root — ostrac: potsherd, shell (Greek ostrakon)

Suffix — -ism

Suffix — -ism: practice or condition

Put it together

Put it together: Ostrac (potsherd, shell — Greek ostrakon) + -ism (practice) = the potsherd practice. Athenians voted a man out of the city by scratching his name on broken pottery, so the shard itself came to name the punishment. The same shell-root floats in oyster, a creature named for its hard plates. Modern ostracism needs no ballot — the group's cold behavior is the vote.

Use the root in a new word: oyster

Use the root in a new word: oyster: The reef's oysters clamp their shells shut the instant a shadow passes over the bed.

Word Choice

formal / analytic

Ostracism is the analyst's word for group-enforced exclusion — sociable animals, playgrounds, and office floors all practice it. It needs no official act; the freeze itself is the punishment. Pariah, taught in this unit, names the person on the receiving end: ostracism is the treatment, a pariah is its target. For one cold incident, snub or slight is enough.
